title: Serving runtime - daily scratchpad (2026-04-04)
content:
Quick notes for 2026-04-04:

Today: triage SRV-2578 (memory leak during long-running KV-cache workloads) + perf runs for kernel fallback path. Short on time - record findings and next actions here.

Top issues:
1) SRV-2578 - memory growth on continuous-batching with KV cache
   - Reported by customer on dedicated cluster: memory climbs ~2-3% per hour until OOM after ~48h under realistic traffic.
   - Suspected area: KV cache glue + attention kernel allocation path when sequence length spikes (seen at ~8k tokens).
   - Linked PR trying initial mitigation: PR#4821 (limits KV index retention for inactive prefixes).

Repro steps (local):
   - checkout serving-runtime@debug-leak
   - start local harness: ./scripts/run_perf_harness.sh --model redwood-7b --batching continuous --kv-cache on --seq-len 8000 --duration 2h
   - monitor: python tools/memwatch.py --pid $(pgrep runtime) --interval 60

Quick logs seen: (excerpt)
   [2026-04-03T22:14:12Z] kv_cache.cpp:allocate_index size=32768 total_indexes=124512 used_mem=2.1GB
   [2026-04-03T23:18:43Z] allocator.cpp:alloc_large returning stale pointer (count++), leak suspected

Hypotheses:
   A) allocator metadata not freed when KV prefix ages out (race between cache eviction and continuous batching threads).
   B) kernel (attention_v2) registers temporary tensors in a per-thread store and doesn't clear on fallback paths.

Immediate experiments to run (short):
   - E1: Instrument allocations for KV index and attention temporary tensors. Add counters + periodic heap dump. (owner: me, ETA EOD)
   - E2: Run harness with JEMALLOC_STATS enabled to see growth pattern per arena. (owner: Liam, ETA tomorrow morning)
   - E3: Reproduce on smaller seq-len (2000) to confirm linear scaling with seq-len. (owner: Priya, ETA today)

Perf TODOs / benchmarks:
   - Baseline: 7b redwood model, continuous batching 128 threads, seq-len 2k, measure tokens/sec and p95 latency.
   - Compare quantized kernels (int8) vs fp16 for long sequences. Notes: quant path shows slightly lower memory but slower attention kernel for >4k tokens (observed).
   - Run perf sweep: batch_size in [8,16,32,64], seq_len in [512,2000,8000], kv_cache [on,off]. Script: ./tools/sweep_perf.sh --out /tmp/sweep-2026-04-04.json

Kernel notes (investigation pointers):
   - attention_v2: check fallback codepath used when token_count % warp_size != 0 - possible allocation not freed on error path.
   - fused_mha kernel: verify workspace_size computation for >4096 context; there was an old fix in release-engineering/patches/patch-2025-12 that might not be applied to dedicated build.

Action items (short):
   - [ ] Add lightweight allocation tracing to KV cache allocator (me) - branch: leak-kv-trace
   - [ ] Ask infra to spin dedicated test cluster with same config as customer (Diego) - include older CUDA driver (12.2) reproducer
   - [ ] Merge quick guard in PR#4821 (limits retention) if initial mem growth stops in local run (Liam to coordinate)
   - [ ] Run long-lived harness for 72h after instrumentation (Priya + me)

Meeting notes / syncs:
   - Quick sync 10:30am with Priya and Liam: align on E1/E2/E3 runs.
   - Scheduling longer triage with SRE and infra on Friday to review kernel-level traces and driver matrix.

Misc notes / ideas:
   - Consider adding a soft cap on per-customer KV index memory with background compaction - buys time while we debug actual leak.
   - Could be worthwhile to add a small GC pass when memory pressure high (scan per-thread stores).

References / links:
   - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821
   - Jira: SRV-2578
   - Confluence: /display/SRV/KV+Cache+Design

Today's quick checklist:
   - [x] reproduce locally with some growth (short run)
   - [ ] instrument allocations (in progress)
   - [ ] start jemalloc run (blocked on infra permissions)

Notes to self: keep logs short and timestamped. If we hit OOM on dedicated cluster again, capture full core dump and contact infra immediately.

End of scratchpad entry.
